title: Kairos backup rule: no window closes in silence
status: PROPOSED, ethereal stage, nothing built; propose-only, Zach rules
one_line: When a timing window is closing and the human trigger has not come, the harness never stays silent. A reversible step may advance on a default declared ahead of time. A one-way door never advances: it escalates, and if the window closes it files a lapse receipt so the miss is a recorded decision, not negligence.

bottom_line.label: The failure
bottom_line.text: Silence, not inaction. A window missed because nobody noticed is negligence. A window passed up on the record is a decision.

bottom_line.label: The rule
bottom_line.text: Two-way door, known close date, declared undo: advance on the declared default and tell Zach. Anything else: stay at the door, escalate as the window closes, and file a lapse receipt at the close.

bottom_line.label: Already true
bottom_line.text: "Merge when green" (PR 1919, PR 1920) is the legitimate backup in miniature: Zach released the door ahead of time with a condition, and the harness only watched the condition. Most windows need a release given early, not machinery.

bottom_line.label: What it adds
bottom_line.text: Two optional backlog row fields (window_closes, default_if_silent), one gate (default_if_silent is refused on a one-way door), one sort in /loops (closing windows first), and one receipt shape (the lapse receipt). No new store, no model calls.

decisions.question: Adopt the rule: an absent trigger never resolves as silence?
decisions.recommended: Yes, as the principle. It costs nothing to state and every later decision hangs on it.
decisions.why: The 2026-10-31 to 11-01 friction (a stale BLOCKED note, PRs merged before the batch reached them) were all silent drift, not wrong actions.

decisions.question: Allow default_if_silent on two-way doors only, with the gate refusing it on one-way doors?
decisions.recommended: Yes. A default on a one-way door is autopilot, which the canon deprecates (ARCS-v9-Chapter-Book-Canon.md:472).
decisions.why: Undo is cheaper than a missed window only when undo exists and was declared before the window, not after.

decisions.question: Make the lapse receipt a decision_receipt row (mode QUICKMOVE, what_unconfirmed naming the ruling that never came)?
decisions.recommended: Yes, the existing table and form. A lapse is a decision by default and the ledger already holds decisions.
decisions.why: A status_note goes stale (the stale BLOCKED note case); the receipt ledger is append-only and the Accountant already reads it.

decisions.question: Should standing conditional releases ("merge when green") be recorded as the preferred kairos backup?
decisions.recommended: Yes: name it in the flight manual as the first thing to ask for when a window has a close date.
decisions.why: It keeps the human trigger and only moves it earlier in time. NOTOMATION holds.

controls.name: Default refused on a one-way door
controls.plain: The backlog gate fails a row that sets default_if_silent while door is one-way or absent.
controls.bad: A row with door one-way and default_if_silent set must fail scripts/backlog_status_check.py --check.
controls.good: A row with door two-way, a rollback and default_if_silent passes.
controls.assay_ready: fixtures to be written first, in backlog_status_check.py --self-test

controls.name: No close in silence
controls.plain: A row whose window_closes is past, still non-terminal, and has no receipt naming it after that date is flagged.
controls.bad: A row with window_closes 2026-10-30, state OPEN, and no receipt must print LAPSED-SILENT.
controls.good: The same row with a lapse receipt dated on or after 2026-10-30 prints nothing.

controls.name: Closing windows sort first
controls.plain: /loops lists rows with a window_closes date before others, nearest first.
controls.bad: A row closing tomorrow listed below one with no date fails the open_loops self-test.

human: When a window has a close date, give the release early and with a condition ("merge when green", "send if they reply by Friday"). That is the backup that keeps the call yours.
If you let a window pass on purpose, say so in one line; the harness files the lapse receipt from it.
A default is only as safe as its undo. If you cannot name the undo, it is a one-way door.
agent: Never advance a one-way door on silence. Escalate, then file the lapse receipt at the close.
Run default_if_silent only when door is two-way, rollback is declared, and the close date has passed; quote the default and the rollback in the receipt.
A conditional release covers only the act and condition it names; a later act needs a new release.
Never call any of this autopilot; the canon deprecates the word. It is NOTOMATION with a declared default.

glossary.plain: The stretch of time when an act is worth more than it is before or after (ADR-081).
The human release a row waits for has not come.
A decision_receipt row saying a window closed without the act or a ruling, so the miss is on the record.
Zach's go given ahead of time with a condition the harness can check, such as "merge when green".
An act that cannot be undone, or whose undo was not declared before it.
